name: LSM6DSL accelerometer & gyroscope
description: STMicroelectronics 6-axis iNEMO IMU: 3-axis accelerometer (±2/4/8/16 g) and 3-axis gyroscope (±125/245/500/1000/2000 dps) plus a die temperature sensor, read over I2C (or SPI). The chip runs on 1.71–3.6 V and its pins are not 5 V tolerant. Sold as: MikroElektronika LSM6DSL Click (MIKROE-2731), a mikroBUS board with two 8-pin headers (AN, RST, CS, SCK, MISO, MOSI, 3V3, GND / PWM, INT, TX, RX, SCL, SDA, 5V, GND), 4.7 kΩ I2C pull-ups to 3.3 V, COMM SEL jumpers that ship set to SPI (move all four to I2C), an INT SEL jumper (INT1/INT2), an ADD SEL jumper (0 = address 0x6A default, 1 = 0x6B) and a power LED.
eli5: Feels which way it is tilted and how fast it is spinning, so your project knows how it is moving.

pins.name: AN
pins.description: mikroBUS analog pin (not connected on this board)

pins.name: RST
pins.description: mikroBUS reset pin (not connected on this board)

pins.name: CS
pins.description: SPI chip select; disconnected in I2C mode (COMM SEL jumpers on I2C tie the chip's CS to 3.3 V)

pins.name: SCK
pins.description: SPI clock; disconnected in I2C mode (COMM SEL on I2C routes the chip's SCL to the SCL pin)

pins.name: MISO
pins.description: SPI data out; disconnected in I2C mode (COMM SEL on I2C sends SDO/SA0 to the ADD SEL jumper)

pins.name: MOSI
pins.description: SPI data in; disconnected in I2C mode (COMM SEL on I2C routes the chip's SDA to the SDA pin)

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V: powers the LSM6DSL (VDD and VDDIO), the SDA/SCL pull-ups and the power LED. Never 5 V

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: mikroBUS PWM pin (not connected on this board)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output, push-pull at 3.3 V: INT1 with the INT SEL jumper on INT1 (default), INT2 on the other side; not needed for basic use

pins.name: TX
pins.description: mikroBUS UART TX (not connected on this board)

pins.name: RX
pins.description: mikroBUS UART RX (not connected on this board)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board); the four COMM SEL jumpers must be on I2C

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board); the four COMM SEL jumpers must be on I2C

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: mikroBUS 5 V rail (not connected on this board); leave unconnected

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Ground (second GND pin, same net as GND)

buildNotes: The Click ships configured for SPI: move all four COMM SEL jumpers (JP1, JP2, JP3, JP5) to the I2C side before use, otherwise the chip never answers on I2C.
Power from the 3V3 pin only (the 5V pin is not connected); the 4.7 kΩ SDA/SCL pull-ups go to 3.3 V, so it is safe on ESP32, Pico and Raspberry Pi.
ADD SEL on 0 (default) gives address 0x6A; on 1 it gives 0x6B (e.g. for a second IMU). Keep both MODE SEL jumpers on 1.

Check WHO_AM_I (register 0x0F) reads 0x6A first (the LSM6DSM reports the same ID); then write CTRL3_C = 0x44 (BDU + auto-increment), CTRL1_XL = 0x40 (104 Hz, ±2 g) and CTRL2_G = 0x40 (104 Hz, ±245 dps). Both sensors are powered down until you do.
Outputs are 16-bit two's complement, low byte first: accel 0x28–0x2D (0.061 mg/LSB at ±2 g), gyro 0x22–0x27 (8.75 mdps/LSB at ±245 dps), temperature 0x20–0x21 (25 °C + raw/256).
The full-scale bits are not in numeric order: FS_XL 01 means ±16 g; gyro FS_G 00/01/10/11 = 245/500/1000/2000 dps (FS_125 bit for ±125 dps).
The temperature output is the die temperature (±15 °C offset), not an air thermometer.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from lsm6dsl import LSM6DSL

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
imu = LSM6DSL(i2c)  # 0x6A: ADD SEL jumper on 0 (default)
while True:
    ax, ay, az = imu.acceleration()
    gx, gy, gz = imu.gyro()
    t = imu.temperature()
    print('A=%.2f,%.2f,%.2fg G=%.1f,%.1f,%.1fdps T=%.1fC' % (ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz, t))
    time.sleep(1)
